title: Future energy demand
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:23Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches energy demand trends, population and technology growth, or predicting future demand; they cover energy conservation, kinetic and potential energy, transfers, and Earth's energy balance.

draft.title: Future energy demand
card: Energy demand is the amount of energy people use. Over the last two centuries it has grown a lot.
Demand grows as the population grows, because more people need electricity, transport and heating. It also grows with new technology, such as air conditioners, computers and electric cars.
Scientists look at trends in past data, such as a line rising each year, to predict future demand. A prediction assumes the trend carries on in a similar way.
If demand keeps rising and is met by burning coal and gas, carbon dioxide emissions will rise too. This is one reason cleaner energy sources are being developed.
draft.remember: Past trends help predict demand, and rising demand drives the search for cleaner energy.

a.q: Which two changes have both helped increase energy demand over time?
opts: More people and more electrical devices
Fewer people and more efficient devices
Cheaper coal and fewer power stations
Less technology and more renewable energy
a.why: More people need more energy, and new devices use extra electricity. The other options each include a change that would lower demand or does not explain it.
a.clue: Think of people and what they plug in.

b.q: A city's electricity use has risen steadily every year for 20 years. A planner says it will probably keep rising. What is the planner's prediction based on?
opts: The trend in past data continuing
A guess that has no link to data
The city running out of coal
The city having fewer people each year
b.why: Predictions about demand use trends in past data and assume they continue. It is not a guess without data. The planner has given no reason to think coal is running out or that the population is falling.
b.clue: What does the 20 years of data show?

a.best: More people and more electrical devices

b.best: The trend in past data continuing
